clue.text: Significant comedian around the South

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so the second word goes inside the first

blocks.note: a comic is a stand-up comedian
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A comedian who matters is touring the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic is used informally of something vast or of huge importance, a loose synonym for significant.

clue.text: Girl left in vehicle is as upset

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the vehicle wraps the letter
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so those two little words get rearranged

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned in a car is understandably distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned, but it is just the single-letter abbreviation that sits inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Female to inform furniture designer

blocks.note: she is the female pronoun
to rat on someone is to inform against them

explanation.surface: A woman is set to betray a furniture maker to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an eighteenth-century English cabinetmaker whose name labels a style of furniture.

clue.text: Suggest just disposing of leader

indicators.note: getting rid of the leader means the opening letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: simply and just are interchangeable, as in 'it's just wrong'

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that we simply get rid of the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLY loses its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to hint at it without stating it, a synonym of suggest.

clue.text: Stumped by foundation garment? I don't believe it!

blocks.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
a roll-on is an elasticated women's girdle, a foundation garment

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a corset exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman can be dismissed 'stumped', written st. STROLL ON is a British exclamation of incredulity.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Stroll on!' is a British idiom voicing astonishment or disbelief, just like the quoted cry.

clue.text: Brontës' play?

blocks.note: surface reading: a drama written by Charlotte, Emily and Anne
setter's reading: the famous literary siblings as a trio give the title of a Chekhov play

explanation.surface: It asks about a stage work by the Brontë family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontës wrote novels, not plays; the play is Chekhov's, whose title happens to describe the Brontës themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's drama about the Prozorov siblings bears a title that also exactly describes the trio of Brontë novelists.

clue.text: Frank, abroad, rung before noon

blocks.note: out and abroad both mean outside, away from home
a spoke is a rung of a ladder or chair
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Frank, overseas, phoned in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rung' looks like the past of ring, a phone call; it is a noun, a ladder's crosspiece.
explanation.definitionFit: An outspoken person speaks their mind openly, which is what being frank means.

clue.text: Rope shown in a trial that's fixed

indicators.note: a fixed contest is rigged, the outcome rearranged dishonestly, so those letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rope is exhibited as evidence in a rigged court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long rope with a running noose used by cowboys.

clue.text: Net lay spread out nicely

indicators.note: things spread out are scattered from their places, so those letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishing net was laid out flat in a pleasing manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something neatly means doing it tidily and well, close in sense to nicely.

clue.text: Drink fizzy pop in ancient city

indicators.note: something fizzy bubbles and churns, so those letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a soft drink while visiting an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo in Syria is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

clue.text: Stupid rioter in Pennsylvania capital

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled and senseless, so those letters are muddled into a new order
one thing in another sits inside it, so the state abbreviation wraps the jumble

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish rioter is loose in a Pennsylvanian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pennsylvania capital' reads as Harrisburg, but the definition is just 'capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital city of South Africa.

clue.text: Runway - one's seen between flights, ahead of take off

blocks.note: a landing is the level area between two flights of stairs
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: A runway is noticed between plane journeys, before departure.
explanation.walkthrough: Flights and take off both pretend to be about aircraft; they are stairs and undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a basic airfield runway where aircraft touch down.

clue.text: Where a customs officer may search, no matter what?

definitions.text: Where a customs officer may search

blocks.clueFragment: Where a customs officer may search
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: inside a piece of luggage
second meaning: regardless, whatever happens

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic description: a customs officer searches in any suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means anyhow, regardless, and read literally also places something inside whichever bag is opened.

clue.text: Gem in pawn taken by nobleman

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for pawn
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat takes a jewel to the pawnshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' suggests pawnbroking; here it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem formed inside an oyster.

clue.text: Saw Tracy, perhaps, making a pudding

blocks.note: spotted and saw both mean noticed
Dick Tracy is the comic-strip detective, so Dick is the name that goes with Tracy

explanation.surface: Seeing someone called Tracy, perhaps while making dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a traditional British dessert, a steamed suet sponge studded with dried fruit.

clue.text: People of the highest standing put up prize trophy

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is slang for a trophy cup

explanation.surface: Elite people offer a trophy as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words together are reversed, pot coming first and reward after it, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest social class; the phrase describes upper-crust people.

clue.text: Smear about leader in industry in column

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
about means surrounding, so the smear goes round the single letter

blocks.note: to plaster is to smear thickly
the opening letter of industry

explanation.surface: Some smear campaign surrounds a captain of industry in a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like journalism but is architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall.

clue.text: Song and dance created by sergeant under fire?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing under another is written below it, so the order of the two parts is fixed

blocks.note: a flame is fire
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier under enemy fire makes a big fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places NCO below FLAME. 'Song and dance' sounds like a fuss, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the Andalusian tradition of passionate song, guitar and dance.

clue.text: Church book in Latin, Pete translated

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so these letters take another shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pete renders a church book into Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' looks like the target of the translating; it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitential is a church manual listing sins and the penances due for them.

clue.text: Rep refurbished marvellous dwelling

indicators.note: refurbishing rebuilds something, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: rearranged
fab is short for fabulous, meaning marvellous

explanation.surface: A sales rep did up a wonderful house.
explanation.walkthrough: A prefab is a prefabricated house, as built in Britain after the war.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a factory-made house assembled on site, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: German boy turned up at home with an old British coin

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Rolf is a German boy's name
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A German lad arrived at the house carrying an antique British coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The florin was the pre-decimal British two-shilling piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British coin worth two shillings, withdrawn after decimalisation.

clue.text: Sovereign measure

blocks.note: first meaning: a monarch who reigns
second meaning: a straight-edged instrument for measuring length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign measure' reads like a royal decree or even a gold coin; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a reigning monarch and the graduated stick used for measuring lengths.

clue.text: Show violence towards powerful member

blocks.note: first meaning: to coerce someone by force
second meaning, read literally: a mighty limb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club or party; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To strong-arm is to bully with physical force, and read literally the phrase is a muscular limb.

clue.text: Navy going on river is pointless

blocks.note: N is an abbreviation for navy
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: Sending the navy up a river would be futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no use serves no purpose, which is what pointless means.

clue.text: Get rid of piece in fountain, say

blocks.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them from a job
a work is a piece, as of art or music

explanation.surface: Someone wants a sculpture removed from a public fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fountain' looks like a water feature; it is a type of firework spraying sparks upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a ground-based firework that sprays a column of sparks, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Boy arrived a moment ago?

blocks.note: first meaning: a boy's name
second meaning, split in two: only recently come in

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the name must be split into two words to fit the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin is a male given name, and read as two words it describes someone who has only now come through the door.

clue.text: Smashed old bust on the rocks

blocks.note: first meaning: broke, financially ruined
second meaning: in severe financial trouble

explanation.surface: A shattered antique bust lies on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a broken statue; 'bust' and 'on the rocks' are both slang for financially ruined, and 'smashed' adds to the picture of being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankrupt person or firm cannot pay its debts, which is what both slang phrases convey.

clue.text: I rowed out to identify queer fish

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or awry, so these letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower goes out on the water to identify an unusual fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer fish' is an old British idiom for an odd person, not a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A queer fish is an eccentric person, and a weirdo is likewise an oddball.
